title: Accurate and Intuitive Contextual Explanations using Linear Model Trees
summary: Proposes LMTE, a local surrogate explainer that fits a linear model tree to synthetic data drawn around the test point, so that a single explanation carries both feature attributions and rules and can follow a non-linear decision boundary that a weighted linear surrogate cannot. CTGAN is the sampling stage the method is built on: the nearest neighbours of the test point are transformed, fed to CTGAN with the discrete columns declared, and the fitted model sampled to produce the locality the surrogate is trained on.
evidence: Table 1 lists the sampling method of the proposed approach as CTGAN, against uniform random for LIME and a genetic algorithm for LORE; section 3.1 states the transformed tabular data is fed to the CTGAN along with the discrete columns so that it can handle them separately, and that test points are sampled from the trained model to give the data generated around the test point's locality; section 3.2 states the synthetic neighbourhood is obtained from the CTGAN before the surrogate is fitted; Figure 3(b) plots the synthetic dataset generated by CTGAN with the decision boundary of the linear model tree fitted to it

title: Detecting Malicious Accounts showing Adversarial Behavior in Permissionless Blockchains
summary: Flags accounts behind malicious activity in permissionless blockchains from temporal and behavioural transaction features, and then asks whether the resulting detectors survive accounts that have been altered to evade them. CTGAN generates that adversarial data: it is fitted separately on each malicious activity class with default parameters and 1000 epochs, and the generated accounts are added to the test set to measure how far detector performance falls.
evidence: Section 2 states that of the GAN variants only CTGan is described because it is the one used to generate fake data for every malicious activity, chosen because it generates tabular data, and records its two fully connected hidden layers, the authors' recommendation of more than 300 epochs, and the limitation that the generator needs at least 10 feature vectors; section 3.3 states CTGan is used to generate adversarial data Dg for the malicious activities and that Dg is used only on the test dataset, with default parameters and 1000 epochs for fitting; the paper spells the model CTGan throughout

title: Effective and Privacy Preserving Tabular Data Synthesizing
summary: A Delft master's thesis that first compares four GAN-based tabular synthesizers on machine learning utility, statistical similarity and privacy, then proposes CTAB-GAN, a conditional table GAN adding a mixed-type encoder, classification and information losses and a DCGAN backbone, and finally extends it to DP-CTABGAN with differentially private training evaluated under membership and attribute inference attacks. CTAB-GAN is built on CTGAN: its mixed-type encoder is derived from CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and it adopts CTGAN's conditional vector and training-by-sampling, while CTGAN is separately one of the four benchmarked baselines, run from the sdv-dev/SDGym code base.
evidence: Section 4.2 states that in CTAB-GAN a Mixed-type Encoder is invented based on the mode-specific normalization introduced in the work of [43], that CTAB-GAN is based on a conditional GAN and utilizes training-by-sampling to treat imbalanced variables, and that it features the classification, information and generator losses; section 2.2.1 reproduces CTGAN's conditional vector construction, generator cross-entropy loss and training-by-sampling procedure in full and attributes all three to [43]; section 2.1.1 credits CTGAN with the conditional architecture, training-by-sampling and mode-specific normalization while noting it cannot handle missing values; section 3.2.2 lists CTGAN as one of four evaluated state-of-the-art baselines, with a footnote giving https://github.com/sdv-dev/SDGym as the code base for all the models; reference [43] resolves to Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni

title: FinGAN: Generative Adversarial Network for Analytical Customer Relationship Management in Banking and Insurance
summary: Attacks class imbalance in banking and insurance analytics two ways: oversampling the minority class with a GAN, and a hybrid that first reduces the majority class to the support vectors found by a one-class SVM before oversampling, tested on churn prediction, auto insurance fraud and loan default with six classifiers and a statistical significance test. CTGAN is one of the three generators run unmodified as the oversampler, and the paper's conclusion rests on it: it forms a headline column of the results tables for all three datasets and the CTGAN-based approaches are the ones reported as best.
evidence: The abstract states Vanilla GAN, Wasserstein GAN and CTGAN are each employed to oversample the minority class; section 3.3.1 states CTGAN was used to produce synthetic data with no changes to its architecture; section 5 attributes CTGAN's superiority over the other two to mode-specific normalization for multiple modes in continuous variables and to training by sampling with conditional generators for unbalanced categorical variables; Tables 7, 9 and 11 give CTGAN and CTGAN+OCSVM columns for churn, insurance fraud and loan default, with CTGAN plus xgboost reported at the best AUC of 0.874 on bank default; the conclusion states that CTGAN based approaches yielded best statistically significant results. pypdf renders some occurrences of the name as CTAGN

title: Experimental Design for Causal Query Estimation in Partially Observed Biomolecular Networks
summary: Gives a simulation-based algorithm for choosing which subset of a partially observed biomolecular network to measure, ranking sub-networks that admit an unbiased causal query estimator by the bias and variance they induce against the differing experimental cost of each variable. CTGAN supplies one of the two synthetic data sources the selection is simulated on: where historical experimental data exist, a tabular GAN is fitted with default hyperparameters and sampled, alongside a Bayesian network forward simulation, and the two are checked against the experimental data on marginal and joint distributions.
evidence: The synthetic data section states that when historical experimental data exist the synthetic data is constructed based on approaches such as Tabular GAN, citing Xu et al. 2019, or on statistical associations such as Bayesian network forward simulation, and that quality is judged by comparing the marginal and joint distributions of the synthetic and experimental data; the case study states that the second synthetic dataset was generated from Tabular GAN, preprocessed as described in Ashrapov 2020 with default hyperparameters; the bibliography resolves Xu et al. 2019 to Modeling tabular data using conditional GAN by Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni

title: Unmasking Trees for Tabular Data
summary: Presents UnmaskingTrees, which fits gradient-boosted decision trees to incrementally unmask individual features for tabular imputation and generation, together with BaltoBot, a balanced-tree conditional density estimator that turns any probabilistic binary classifier into a generative model, and reports leading imputation performance on a 27-dataset out-of-the-box benchmark. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the compared generators: the paper repeats the experimental setup of Jolicoeur-Martineau et al. and reports their average ranks across nine metrics both on complete data and under 20 percent missingness.
evidence: Section 3.2 states the paper repeats the experimental setup of Jolicoeur-Martineau et al. 2024b on the same 27 datasets, whose benchmark compares Gaussian Copula, tabular variational autoencoding (TVAE) and the conditional GAN methods CTGAN and CTAB-GAN+ against two diffusion methods under nine metrics in the fully observed and 20 percent MCAR settings; the two ranking tables report TVAE and CTGAN rows alongside UnmaskingTrees on Wtrain, Wtest, coverage, R2fake, F1fake, F1disc, Pbias and covrate. A GaussianCopula row appears in the same tables but the paper attributes it to Joe 2014 rather than to SDV, so only CTGAN and TVAE are recorded here

title: TAEGAN: Generating Synthetic Tabular Data For Data Augmentation
summary: Introduces TAEGAN, a tabular GAN whose generator is a masked auto-encoder given a self-supervised warmup and a weight-matrix-based sampling scheme, and reports that on small datasets it improves machine learning efficacy over larger language-model-based generators. It inherits CTGAN's feature engineering, one-hot categorical encoding and variational Gaussian mixture decomposition of continuous columns following mode-specific normalization, and generalizes CTGAN's conditional vector into a representation that lifts the restriction to categorical components and to a single component per condition; CTGAN and TVAE are separately two of the seven baselines, run from synthcity, and the reality and fidelity metrics follow the SDMetrics documentation.
evidence: Section 3 states TAEGAN inherits feature engineering from CTGAN, one-hot encoding categorical features and decomposing continuous features with VGM following mode-specific normalization in Xu et al. 2019; the same section introduces a new conditional vector representation compatible with different prior works, noting that CTGAN allows only components from categorical features and that prior works constrain exactly one component to be maintained in the condition, whereas TAEGAN allows all; appendix C.2 gives the Synthcity implementation as the source for CTGAN and TVAE; the metrics paragraph cites Dat 2023, listed in the bibliography as Synthetic Data Metrics, DataCebo, Inc., https://docs.sdv.dev/sdmetrics/, version 0.13.0, for the reality and fidelity definitions and cites Xu et al. 2019 for the machine learning efficacy metric; Tables 2 and 3 and Figure 2 report CTGAN, CTAB-GAN+ and TVAE against TAEGAN

title: Diffusion-nested Auto-Regressive Synthesis of Heterogeneous Tabular Data
summary: Proposes TABDAR, an auto-regressive transformer for heterogeneous tabular data in which continuous columns are handled by a nested diffusion head and column order is randomized through masked training, so one model serves unconditional generation, arbitrary conditional generation and imputation. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the ten compared generators, run from the TabSyn code base and reported on marginal and joint fidelity, alpha-precision, beta-recall, a classifier two-sample test and downstream machine learning efficacy across ten datasets.
evidence: Section 5.1 lists TVAE and CTGAN, both cited to Xu et al. 2019, as the VAE-based and GAN-based entries among ten baselines drawn from six categories; appendix D.5 states that the implementations of CTGAN and TVAE follow the codebase of Zhang et al. 2024b; Table 1 reports their marginal, joint, alpha-precision, beta-recall, C2ST and JSD scores and Table 2 their downstream AUC and RMSE, both against TABDAR; the metrics appendix footnotes https://docs.sdv.dev/sdmetrics/metrics/metrics-in-beta/detection-single-table for the detection metric
